title: Spectral Prefill Orchestrator: bandwidth-aware rendezvous and kernel hinting for multi-GPU prefill/decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce 99th-percentile prefill+decode latency for multi-GPU tensor/pipeline-parallel workloads by improving rendezvous timing, adaptive NCCL overlap windows, and kernel selection hints.

Background: We observe tail latency spikes when prefill and decode phases interleave on heterogeneous device topologies. Current rendezvous is reactive and coarse-grained: microbatches synchronize at fixed points leading to bandwidth contention and suboptimal kernel choices for attention (cuBLAS vs fused attention kernels). Recent profiling (see attachments) shows: (1) KV cache copies + nccl all-to-all peaks correlate with decode latency spikes, (2) attention compute kernel latency varies with sequence-length distribution and co-running prefill traffic.

Scope: Implement a coordinator we call the Spectral Prefill Orchestrator (SPO) that: (a) maintains a short-term bandwidth/pending-comm spectrum per device, (b) exposes a kernel-hint API to select attention kernels based on current comm/compute mix, and (c) schedules rendezvous windows to overlap NCCL communication opportunistically with low-latency compute phases. This work sits in the serving runtime orchestrator and scheduler layers and will include microbenchmarks, simulator, and canary rollout on dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce prefill+decode P99 latency by >= 18% on internal Llama-variant benchmark with 64-token prefill and 512-token decode compared to baseline (no SPO)
No regression (>2%) in median latency on small batch conversational workloads
End-to-end correctness retained (no model output divergence) across 1000 deterministic eval traces
Unit and integration tests covering rendezvous state machine, kernel-hint API, and bandwidth estimator are present
Canary rollout with automated rollback rule configured in console for runtime-1.21
implementation_tasks: Design and document SPO state model and APIs (rendezvous epochs, slot weights, hint tokens) - design doc PR: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/SPO-Design
Implement device-local bandwidth estimator (exponential moving average of issued NCCL bytes + observed throughput) and expose via lightweight shared-memory ring
Add kernel-hint API in runtime dispatcher: hintPreference {prefer_fused_attention, prefer_matmul_cublas, prefer_sparse_path} and integrate with kernel selector
Rendezvous windowing: implement slot-weighted rendezvous broker that can delay or advance sync points by up to 1 microbatch to create overlap opportunities
Integrate with prefill microbatch allocator to support progressive KV siphoning (evict+streaming of hot KV shards) to reduce instantaneous comm peaks
Simulator: extend token-flow simulator to model NCCL overlap and test heuristics at scale (up to 128 GPUs)
Add telemetry: fine-grained per-token comm/compute timeline traces, rendezvous decisions, kernel hint metrics
End-to-end benchmarks and PR to runtime repo (github): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/XXXX
testing_plan: Microbenchmarks: isolated KV-copy, all-to-all, and attention kernel latencies across seq lengths and device counts
A/B cluster tests: run baseline vs SPO on dedicated dev pool for 48 hours under synthetic conversational load (1000 qps) and collect perf counters
Deterministic output regression tests on 1k traces before/after applying kernel hints
Stress test combined prefill+decode bursts with artificial network jitter to validate graceful degradation and rollback
Run end-to-end CI with new unit/integration tests and simulate failure scenarios (e.g., partial NCCL failure, unexpected device slowdowns)
rollout_plan: Feature flag gate for SPO; off by default
Internal canary: enable SPO on dedicated non-production pool (10% of internal traffic) for 72h
Staged ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over two weeks with automated rollback if P99 rises by >5%
Expose runtime tunables in Console: rendezvous_max_shift, bandwidth_smoothing_window_ms, kernel_hint_mode
Post-rollout validation: daily job comparing P50/P95/P99 against baseline and reporting to #runtime-performance channel
